title: streaming-backpressure-and-compat-layer-contenttype-guards-with-tool-payload-throttle
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: Several recent incidents and internal customer reports highlighted two recurring issues: (1) multipart file uploads used by tool/function-calling flows could cause unbounded memory/queue growth when clients stream faster than worker throughput; (2) the OpenAI-compatibility layer did not consistently enforce content-type and structured-output size constraints which allowed oversized tool payloads to propagate to downstream runners. This PR introduces coordinated protections across the API entrypoint and compatibility shim to make streaming uploads more resilient and to place deterministic limits on tool/file payloads. Summary of changes: - Add streaming backpressure checks at the multipart parser level: per-connection in-flight byte quotas, configurable low/high watermarks, and early 413-style rejections when quotas are exceeded. This prevents request buffering at the gateway and gives predictable failure semantics for fast clients. - Introduce a "X-Tool-Payload-Quota" header that the compat layer will return in streaming responses for tool-calls; the header communicates server-allocated byte budget and remaining allowance so clients can adapt backoff behavior. - Implement server-side throttling for tool file payloads: if a tool upload exceeds its negotiated quota, the server will gracefully terminate the stream and emit structured diagnostics (JSON body with quota_used and limit). - Tighten content-type validation on the OpenAI compatibility endpoint: accept only a small whitelist (multipart/form-data, application/json, application/octet-stream) for attachments and reject ambiguous types (e.g., text/plain with non-UTF8). Also normalize and strip suspicious charset parameters. - Add structured-output size guard for function/tool-calls: the runtime will enforce a serialized size cap for tool responses when wired through the compat layer, with fallback policy support (truncate / error / partial-result). - Add tests (unit + integration) that simulate fast-producer slow-consumer streaming and verify quotas, header propagation, and diagnostic payloads. - Docs and changelog entries for the new headers and configuration knobs. Backwards compatibility: default quotas are conservative and can be raised by config; compat-layer behavior keeps response format stable and only adds the optional header. There is a brief note in CHANGELOG about a new rejected response shape for quota failures so customers can detect and surface them. See release_notes for details. Implementation notes: The backpressure implementation sits in the multipart parser middleware so it applies to both native API routes and the OpenAI-compat gateway. The quota enforcement is per-upload part and per-connection aggregated; we added metrics for quota_rejections, quota_bytes_consumed, and compat_header_emitted. We preferred early reject semantics to avoid head-of-line blocking in the request pipeline. Why this is different from earlier multipart commits: earlier PRs focused on content sniffing and chunking semantics; this PR focuses on operational protection (memory/queue) and explicit client feedback for throttling, plus a small-but-important compat-layer content-type whitelist and structured output cap.

review_comments: Evan Turner: Can we avoid adding another global config var? Suggest scoping quota defaults per-route so Hosted customers aren't affected by Private installs.
Priya Desai (author): Scoped the default into route-level config with a global fallback; updated docs and added config examples.
Marta Iqbal: Tests look good. Add an assertion that the quota header is present on partial failures too (helps clients detect retryability).
Priya Desai (author): Added test and a small fix to header emission on error paths.
Rafael Gomez: Small nit: normalizeContentType should treat application/octet-stream; also ensure charset parameters are stripped for comparisons.
Priya Desai (author): Done. Added normalization unit test.
release_notes: Added server-side streaming quotas for multipart uploads to avoid request buffering; introduced X-Tool-Payload-Quota header to communicate remaining upload budget; compat layer now enforces a strict content-type whitelist for attachments and a serialized structured-output size cap for tool responses. Default quotas are conservative and configurable. Clients should handle 413-like quota rejections by backing off and honoring the header.
notes_for_ops: Config knobs: multipart.quota.default_bytes, multipart.quota.high_watermark, compat.tool_response.max_serialized_bytes. Metrics: quota_rejections, quota_bytes_consumed, compat_header_emitted. Recommend enabling alert on quota_rejections > 0.1% of multipart requests in first 24h after rollout.
